_about: Warnings on vNext journeys that a person reviewed and accepted, with the reason. The validator counts vNext warnings not listed here as unreviewed. `match` is an optional substring of the message.

reviews.note: t2 (at-risk notice) and t3 (reminder) are the two exclusive arms of c.critical - a critical prerequisite is either missing or it is not. They are never sent together; no simultaneous rule is needed.
Adoption nurture ends only in handoffs by design: stable adoption goes to the lifecycle owner, a stall goes to adoption recovery. There is no outcome it owns alone.

Renewal reminder ends only in handoffs by design: a decided renewal executes (SUB-164), a non-renewal schedules its end (SUB-168), an undefined term or an overrun review goes to decision or ownership. The decision is the outcome and each decision has an owner.
Renewal payment recovery is a relationship-state holder: it ends in completion, end or decision resolution, all owned elsewhere. Its communication is FIN-134's.
The acknowledgement deliberately carries no route: there is nothing to rebook onto, and a rebooking prompt with nothing behind it is the false call to action the journey forbids.
t-offer and t-ack are the two exclusive arms of c.rebookable - rebooking is available or it is not. Never both.

t-old and t-new are both sent, in sequence, to two different destinations: the replaced destination is warned, then the new destination is asked to confirm. This is the two-party confirmation itself, not a simultaneous send to one person's channels; the channel is the destination's own kind.
Route assignment chooses a path and hands over: blocked start to ACT-13, clear start to ACT-12. It owns no outcome of its own.
t1 (specific action to the account) and t2 (raise with the dependency owner) are the exclusive arms of c.self-resolvable. Never both.
The corpus's own rule: success is a meaningful return - a real action in the product - never an open or a click. The event is inspected (a.inspect) before anything advances.
Interest routing ends in a handoff on every path by design: a named destination, a disqualifier, or education.
High-intent routing decides who owns the next step and hands to them: an assigned person, automated continuation, or the already-reached destination.
The stability check owns only the observation: sustained recovery hands to the lifecycle owner, relapse hands back to diagnosis.
t1 (a person will follow up) and t2 (deliver the material) are the exclusive arms of c.declared - what the person asked for. Never both.
t1 (in product) and t2 (surviving off-product route) are the exclusive arms of c.route - what can carry the repair request. Never both.
The confirmation states that the replacement is in use; it asks for nothing and carries no route by design.
The light and heavy asks are the exclusive arms of c.type - the size of request the evidence supports.
The information request and the outcome statement are the exclusive arms of c.outcome (MORE_INFORMATION_REQUIRED vs a conclusion).
The customer request and the internal request are the exclusive arms of c.provider - who can supply the item.
The discharge confirmation asks for nothing; it closes the loop and carries no route by design.
The restricted notice and the quiet notice are the exclusive arms of c.restricted - whether grace reduces anything the holder will notice.
The recovery confirmation asks for nothing; it names what returned and carries no route by design.
The four route statements are the exclusive arms of c.route - which mechanism restores validity. Exactly one is ever sent.
The confirmation of restored validity asks for nothing and carries no route by design.
The restoration confirmation asks for nothing; it names what returned and carries no route by design.
The first-time notice and the brief confirmation are the exclusive arms of c.first-time. Never both.
The brief confirmation to a familiar holder names only what changed and carries no route by design.
The restoration confirmation asks for nothing; it names what was invalidated and carries no route by design.
The known-holder and new-counterparty invitations are the exclusive arms of c.known. Never both.
The activation confirmation to both sides names scope and direction and carries no route by design.
The non-recoverable notice (t2) and the recoverable blocker (t4) are the exclusive arms of c.blockers.
The closure confirmation states what closed and what closure is not; it asks for nothing by design.
Full and partial closure records are the exclusive arms of c.outcome.
The closure record is the durable answer to the request; it asks for nothing by design.
Partial and total notices are the exclusive arms of c.scope - how much of the connection is affected.
The restoration confirmation names what came back and carries no route by design.
The active confirmation and the generic failure are the exclusive arms of c.outcome.
The credential, permission and capability fixes are the exclusive arms of c.stage - exactly one stage failed.
The active confirmation names the validated capabilities and carries no route by design.
Allocation decides whether resources exist and hands to reservation or to cancellation reconciliation.
Every resolution of an exception belongs to execution, delay handling or cancellation reconciliation.
A delay ends in resumption, an exception, a cancellation or ownership escalation - all owned elsewhere.
The executor's report decides the next journey: confirmation, failed-attempt recovery or delay.
A failed attempt ends in a retry dispatch, a return or an exception - all owned elsewhere.
A correction ends in verification, an alternative remedy or ownership escalation.

Rejection notice, review acknowledgement, human review and approval share c.eligible's prerequisites: rejection, review and approval are its exclusive arms, and the acknowledgement follows the review step.
The under-review acknowledgement states a state without implying an outcome; it asks for nothing by design.
The no-choice update and the offer are the exclusive arms of c.choice.
The arrival confirmation states the evidence of delivery and asks for nothing; the acceptance request that may follow carries the route.
The accept and decline confirmations are the exclusive arms of c.answer.
A confirmation or lapse notice closes the offer and asks for nothing by design; the offer and reminder carried the route.
A confirmation or lapse notice closes the offer and asks for nothing by design; the offer and reminder carried the route.
A confirmation or lapse notice closes the offer and asks for nothing by design; the offer and reminder carried the route.
Rejection notice, authorisation notice and human review are the exclusive arms of c.eligible.
The discharge confirmation and the overdue notice are the exclusive arms of c.settled at the deadline.
The cancellation confirmation states the end date and what remains; it asks for nothing by design and never re-litigates.
The reallocation notice tells the customer what changed while the time stands; it asks for nothing by design.
Confirmation, re-offer and decline are the exclusive arms of c.outcome - what revalidation decided.
The nearest-window offer and the waitlist offer are the exclusive arms of c.options.
The external request and the internal request are the exclusive arms of c.source-type - who holds the information.
The cleared confirmation names what the decision no longer affects; it asks for nothing by design.
Correctable, reapplicable and final are the exclusive arms of c.path - exactly one is true.
Self-offer and holder-offer are the exclusive arms of c.decider; the blocked-party notice follows the holder-offer in sequence.
The actionable and standing notices are the exclusive arms of c.usable - whether the entitlement is exercised or held.
The hold notice and the blocker prompt are the exclusive arms of c.resolvable.

Surfaced by the Runtime Mechanism gap-closure round giving CON-36 a real entity.instanceKey (contact_point_id) for the first time. Not a defect this round's fix introduced: ACC-261's h.unreachable fires once every permitted route has been exhausted, not against one specific contact point, so it structurally cannot carry a single contact_point_id - each individual destination's own UNDELIVERABLE transition already reaches CON-36 separately via its own t.contactability trigger. This handoff is escalation/context for a person-level exhaustion finding, which CON-36's own design deliberately has no single-identity entry point for (see CON-36's own guardrail: no person-level reachable flag). Left as a documented, reviewed gap rather than forcing an invented contact_point_id onto a handoff that does not have one; resolving it properly would mean either CON-36 gaining an aggregate/person-scoped view or ACC-261 iterating per destination, both out of this round's scope (do not invent data, do not add canonical topology to satisfy a validator).

Same finding and same reasoning as ACC-261's h.unreachable, above - an independent instance of the identical shape (all permitted routes exhausted, no single contact_point_id to carry) into the same target.
